headline: Scott names four leaders for Vermont agencies as roles shift across state government
dek: The appointments put new deputies in Vermont’s human-services and commerce agencies, elevate a longtime budget official in human resources and move tourism leadership into an interim phase.
body: Gov. Phil Scott has appointed four leaders to senior roles in Vermont state government, changing the management teams at the departments responsible for human resources, human services, commerce and tourism. The announcement affects the state’s central administrative operations as well as agencies that shape services for families and the economy, according to the [governor’s announcement](https://governor.vermont.gov/press-release/governor-phil-scott-announces-leadership-appointments-5) and independent reporting by [Vermont Business Magazine](https://vermontbiz.com/news/2026/september/30/governor-scott-announces-leadership-appointments-kramer-nolan-pelham).

Nick Kramer was named deputy commissioner of the Department of Human Resources. Scott’s office said Kramer had been chief operating officer of the Agency of Administration, where he worked across the departments of Finance and Management, Human Resources, Taxes, Buildings and General Services, Libraries, Financial Services and the Office of Racial Equity. Before joining that role in 2024, he worked in the Department of Finance and Management on state operating and capital budgets.

Shabnam Nolan was appointed deputy secretary of the Agency of Human Services, which coordinates major state programs serving Vermonters. Nolan has led King Street Center in Burlington since 2021. The governor’s office said her work there included youth workforce development, mentoring, early-childhood and after-school programming, and family supports. Nolan is scheduled to begin Oct. 19, taking the position previously held by Kristin McClure, who is now commissioner of Human Resources.

The two appointments connect administrative management with the state’s human-services system at a time when Vermont agencies are managing workforce and service pressures. The announcement does not set out new programs or funding. Its immediate effect is organizational: Kramer brings experience in state budgeting and agency operations to the human-resources department, while Nolan brings nonprofit and community-program experience into the Agency of Human Services.

Scott also appointed Heather Pelham deputy secretary of the Agency of Commerce and Community Development. Pelham had served as commissioner of the Department of Tourism and Marketing since 2019. In that job, the governor’s office credited her with overseeing tourism promotion and the use of $10.4 million in federal EDA-ARPA Travel, Tourism and Outdoor Recreation funding intended to support economic recovery after the pandemic.

The tourism department will be led on an interim basis by Sara DeFilippi, who was named interim commissioner after Pelham’s move. DeFilippi has spent eight years with the department and most recently served as director of partnerships and community engagement, according to the state. Her duties have included outreach to tourism businesses and community organizations, relocation efforts through the Grants for Relocation Outreach Work program, and international marketing activities.

The state’s public directory lists Pelham under the Agency of Commerce and Community Development and identifies DeFilippi with the tourism department, providing a current administrative reference as the changes take effect. The directory also shows how the appointments fit into the existing structure: tourism remains a department within the broader commerce agency, while the human-resources and human-services roles sit in separate parts of state government. The [Vermont Business Magazine report](https://vermontbiz.com/news/2026/september/30/governor-scott-announces-leadership-appointments-kramer-nolan-pelham) independently identifies the four appointments and their titles.

The leadership changes will be measured by what the agencies do next, not simply by the appointments themselves. For Human Resources, that means how the department supports the state workforce and carries out administrative responsibilities. For Human Services, Commerce and Tourism, the practical questions include how leaders maintain ongoing programs, coordinate with local and nonprofit partners, and turn existing plans into services and economic activity. Scott’s announcement provides the personnel changes; future agency updates will show their policy and operational effects.
author: NorthEast News Desk
